title: the T.35 payload buffer was allocated to its exact size, so a padded reader ran past it
lifetime_ender: NONE -- the buffer is alive throughout. SPATIAL row.
shape: a reader that may read up to AV_INPUT_BUFFER_PADDING_SIZE past the payload runs off an exactly sized allocation
allocator_layer: the platform allocator itself: one direct av_buffer_alloc, no inner layer.
fidelity: model consumer, real constant. AV_INPUT_BUFFER_PADDING_SIZE is FFmpeg's own 64, and the case asserts that the unpadded allocation ends before the padded read does.
live_proof: absent at the pin: n9.0.1:libavcodec/cbs_av1_syntax_template.c carries av_buffer_alloc(current->payload_size + AV_INPUT_BUFFER_PADDING_SIZE) together with the memset of that padding. The pre-fix line, av_buffer_alloc(current->payload_size), is at 8553e6ef57^ and is absent from the pin. A fix-reversal.

spatial.oracle: PREDICTED, not measured: added after this corpus's last platform run. The crossing leaves a direct allocation, so a per-allocation bound SHOULD fault. On CheriBSD that is conditional on the usable size for this request -- a size class is a step function and the capability length must be read in-guest before the arm is called either way.

status: built 2026-10-08; native arms measured by runners/run-native.sh in the same commit. The platform arms are declared predictions.
nested_why: the crossed buffer came straight from av_buffer_alloc with no inner allocator between it and the platform, so under this inventory's axis -- WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT -- this row is NOT nested.
distinguishing: the other rows here cross by a mis-shaped index; this one crosses because the allocation omits padding that FFmpeg's own readers are documented to require, so the index is correct and the SIZE is wrong.
